content.text: § 22 is the only audit right, and no monitoring/verification right elsewhere undercuts it. It matches the preferred position on every material term.

input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
input.rationale: § 22 is the only usage audit/verification right binding us; a document-wide search for audit, inspection, monitoring, verification, remote access and telemetry language surfaced nothing else that could expand it. The clause meets the preferred position on every material term: frequency is capped at once in any twelve-month period, notice is thirty days' prior written notice, audits are limited to normal business hours and to licence-quantity compliance, and they must be off-site where practicable and conducted by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality. § 22.2 puts audit costs on Vendor unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent (the preferred 5% trigger, not the 10% fallback), and it expressly bars Vendor and its auditor from accessing Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information — so the walk-away risks of unlimited/unannounced audits and remote system access are excluded. § 22.3 adds customer-favourable protections (findings are our Confidential Information, use limited to enforcing the Agreement, copy of the final report, and payment of a shortfall resolves the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error). No redline required.
